Notice that, by definition, the Bayesian MSL (n) Lmin is obtained by minimising over POVMs acting collectively on n copies, dubbed “correlated measurements” in Ref. [95]. Despite increasing efforts in the experimental implementation of few-copy collective measurements [151, 153, 156–160], scaling them to large n remains challenging in practice. Following this observation, recent work in local QET has addressed the minimum multiparameter frequentist loss achievable with single-copy measurements and classical feedback, referred to as “uncorrelated measurements” in Ref. [95]. This quantity corresponds to a minimisation of the weighted trace of the inverse Fisher information matrix (FIM) over all single-copy POVMs, Lmin (θ) := min Tr[LF (θ)−1 ], restricting each copy to be measured independently, albeit adaptively with classical feedback from previous outcomes. Therefore, we expect that imposing an analogous restriction in the Bayesian case should lead to a similar behaviour as the number of shots increases.
